# FAQ-023 Engineering FAQ #23

Revision: Rev A

Q1: What lubricant should be used for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02), and why?

A1: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-426 for EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Rationale: this lubricant has been qualified for the metallurgical environment and temperature profile specific to the furnace cavity design used on this line. Background testing referenced in SB-1016 established compatibility with furnace internal seals and conveyor components, reducing deposit formation and maintaining thermal conductivity where required. Example application: apply the product at specified touch-up points during scheduled maintenance per SOP-P2-L4-03 to maintain sliding contact surfaces and prevent galling. Records to keep: log the part number, batch or lot identifier from the supplier, quantity issued to the asset, technician initials, and the maintenance checklist entry referencing SOP-P2-L4-03. Retain a copy of the supplier technical data sheet with the equipment file and attach a cross-reference to SB-1016 for qualification notes.

Q2: What blast wheel liner bolt torque is required for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03), and how should it be applied?

A2: The blast wheel liner bolt torque for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 is 90 N·m. Rationale: liner retention hardware must be torqued to this value to ensure clamping without overstressing the liner or bolt threads, maintaining wheel balance and minimizing loosening under cyclic loading. Application procedure: use a calibrated torque tool set to the specified value and perform a star pattern progression to seat the liner uniformly. Background: torque value is derived from fastener grade and liner material properties as documented in SB-1016 and implemented in SOP-P3-L1-05. Examples of records: record the bolt torque check in the preventive maintenance record, note the torque tool serial or calibration identifier, and document any deviations with photographic evidence if liners show uneven wear or fastener damage. Maintain records in the equipment maintenance folder and reference SB-1016 for original design calculations.

Q3: What is the system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03), and what are the implications for operation?

A3: The system pressure limit for EQ-P2-L4-HP03 is 320 bar. Rationale: this limit reflects the maximum safe working pressure of the hydraulic circuit components used on this press, including hoses, seals, and the main pressure relief valve. Operating within the limit prevents overstress, seal extrusion, and sudden component failure. Implementation guidance: ensure pressure readings are monitored using calibrated gauges and that relief circuitry is verified during start-up checks as directed in SOP-P2-L4-03. If pressure approaches the limit, stop operations and perform a leak and condition inspection per the SOP. Records to keep: log gauge readings at start-up and at completion of shift, record relief valve setpoint verification, and retain any fault reports generated when pressure excursions are detected. Cross-reference inspection findings with SB-1016 for component specification and maintenance history.

Q4: Which lubricant part number is specified for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02), and what handling practices are required?

A4: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-278 for EQ-P3-L1-SB02. Rationale and background: CFW-LUB-278 has been selected for compatibility with the media and wheel materials used in the hot forge shot blast cabinet environment. It minimizes fling-off, resists breakdown under abrasive loading, and limits transfer to forged parts where possible. Handling practices: store the lubricant in the original container, protect it from contamination, and issue it to technicians in measured quantities. Apply in accordance with the dispensing steps in SOP-P3-L1-05 to avoid over-application that could affect blast effectiveness. Records to keep: retain issuance records including part number, container lot, issuing technician, and the maintenance task reference to SOP-P3-L1-05. Maintain a traceable link to SB-1016 for historical selection rationale.

Q5: What main ram bolt torque is required for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03), and what verification steps are recommended?

A5: The main ram bolt torque for EQ-P3-L3-HP03 is 1600 N·m. Rationale: the main ram retention hardware must be torqued to this value to assure axial clamping and alignment under machining forces and to prevent relative movement that could induce chatter or misalignment. Verification steps: use a calibrated torque wrench or hydraulic torque unit capable of the specified value, confirm calibration identifiers on the tool, and perform torque application in a controlled sequence to ensure uniform load distribution. If any fastener cannot be torqued to the specified value due to damaged threads or tool limitation, do not proceed with operation; escalate per SOP-P2-L4-03 for corrective action. Records to keep: document torque application in the machine maintenance log, include tool calibration reference, technician initials, and note any re-torquing intervals performed. Retain a copy of the verification report and link it to the equipment file and to SB-1016 for design support.

Related documents: SB-1016, SOP-P2-L4-03, SOP-P3-L1-05

End of document.
